source_snapshot.procedure: Verify normal host state, ping OS-IP, have an operator press the physical system-reset button, observe system reset and require recovery in 10-15 minutes; generic setup asks to clear logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Contradictorily require the BMC-reset button, BMC reset, BMC-IP outage and BMC-IP recovery.
source_snapshot.script: No script; 15 attended and 15 machine minutes.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; correctly reserves physical button action for a person but misses the System-versus-BMC reset and OS-IP-versus-BMC-IP conflict.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at CRITICAL risk; resolve reset semantics, drain workload, press once under approval and collect independent host/BMC evidence.

old_problem: Procedure and Criteria specify different physical controls, reset domains and reachability oracles. A system reset normally targets the ComputerSystem/host and OS-IP, while a BMC reset targets the management controller and BMC-IP; the unaffected plane may remain available. Monitoring both after a press cannot retroactively determine which mutually inconsistent objective was authoritative, and a wrong button press is a critical disruptive action.
disposition_reason: Retain Engineering Decision Pending and Source Conflict. DMTF Redfish defines ComputerSystem.Reset and Manager.Reset as separate resource actions, corroborating that system and management-controller resets are distinct standard domains. ED-17/ED-25 keep the physical button human-operated, but no approved decision chooses the source's competing branch. The owner must identify the exact button, intended reset domain and OS/BMC reachability matrix before one disruptive press. Workload, IP, deadline and observer values are parameterizable, so the case is not inherently BLOCKED.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1741, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 record, pending/conflict analyses, duplicate identity result and ED-01 through ED-30 rules were read. The actual next formal queue identity was reconstructed and directly opened as Functionality row 1754 / Wistron-HW-00387-V003 / ab9fd4e62e1b1a80.

DMTF's standard data model gives `ComputerSystem.Reset` an action on the system resource and `Manager.Reset` an action that resets/reboots the manager. This supports separate outage domains; it does not choose which physical panel button this project intended.

The Procedure's system-reset/OS-IP branch and Criteria's BMC-reset/BMC-IP branch can produce opposite reachability states. Silent merging would allow the wrong action to pass against the wrong oracle.

Physical press, button identification and LED/console observation remain authorized-operator tasks. Automation may only prepare baselines and collect synchronized OS-IP, BMC-IP, console, BMC health and preserved-log evidence.

Because a system reset can interrupt workloads and lose volatile data, approval requires maintenance window, workload drain, backups/recovery readiness and independent observer. No API/SSH reset substitutes for the physical-button objective.
The 10-15 minute source window is preserved but cannot become PASS authority until the owner confirms it for the selected reset type. ED-18 forbids inventing a replacement deadline.
ED-19 excludes pre-test log clearing, ED-26 forbids a second press or power-cycle retry, and no DUT/reset action was executed.

test_case.test_name: Physical reset button — unresolved system versus BMC target with dual-plane timeline
test_case.purpose: After an owner selects the authoritative reset type and physical control, validate one approved button press against a signed host/BMC outage-and-recovery matrix while protecting workloads and retaining synchronized OS, management, console, LED and log evidence.
required_package: Written ruling selecting System Reset/OS-IP, BMC Reset/BMC-IP or separately accepted checkpoints, with exact button/panel mapping and expected unaffected plane
Exact SUT/BMC/firmware/OS identity, OS-IP/BMC-IP and signed before/during/recovery state matrix for host, manager, console, LEDs and services
Approved recovery deadline including disposition of the source 10-15 minute window, packet interval/loss semantics and clock synchronization
Maintenance/workload-drain approval, data protection/backup confirmation, authorized physical operator, independent observer and recovery console
Read-only dual-plane ping/health/log collector, timestamped photo/video evidence path and platform/BMC escalation procedure
test_case.test_command: DO NOT EXECUTE until the written reset ruling and critical-action approval exist. Drain/protect workloads, verify exact target/button and capture healthy OS-IP, BMC-IP, console, service, LED and preserved-log baselines. Start synchronized independent monitoring; the authorized operator photographs the control and presses it exactly once. Record both reachability planes, console/LED/reset events and recovery through the signed deadline, then verify selected and unaffected domains plus services. Do not clear logs, let the agent press hardware, substitute API/SSH reset, press again or power-cycle.
test_case.expected_result: The single approved physical press produces exactly the signed reset-domain signature: selected-plane outage/reset and recovery, explicitly defined behavior of the other plane, correct console/LED events and healthy post-recovery services within the approved deadline. No unintended domain, boot loop, data/service corruption or unplanned configuration change occurs, and complete pre/during/post evidence remains preserved.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: Review remains PENDING until button/target/oracle authority is signed. After binding, PASS requires the exact one-press dual-plane timeline, physical evidence, selected-domain recovery and unaffected-domain behavior defined by that matrix. A ping drop alone, only OS-IP or BMC-IP, eventual recovery without deadline, API reset or repeated press is insufficient. Wrong outage domain, unsafe workload impact, timeout, boot loop, missing evidence or recovery action is reported for engineer FAIL/BLOCKED disposition; the end user decides the verdict.
safety_gate: Do not press any control until system-versus-BMC semantics, exact panel button and expected dual-plane states are approved.
Drain workloads, preserve data and require explicit critical-action authorization plus an independent observer and recovery path.
Only the authorized operator presses once; the agent must not touch hardware or substitute remote/API reset.
Do not clear SEL/dmesg/syslog, press again, issue reset/power commands or power-cycle to force recovery; preserve first failure evidence.
Stop/escalate on wrong button/domain, unexpected loss of both planes, boot loop, unsafe state or deadline expiry.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/Variant, written reset-target ruling, button mapping, signed dual-plane oracle and recovery deadline
SUT/BMC/firmware/OS identities, OS-IP/BMC-IP, workload-drain/data-protection approval, operator/observer and synchronized clocks
Physical button/LED photo or video and one-press timestamp correlated to OS/BMC ping, console, health and reset events
Complete preserved pre/during/post SEL/dmesg/syslog/service evidence and recovery-duration/outage-scope comparison
No-substitution/no-second-press/no-power-cycle audit, exceptions/recovery and engineer-owned PENDING/PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict
test_case.recovery: On wrong domain, unexpected outage, boot loop, service/data concern or deadline expiry, stop monitoring only after evidence is secured and do not press/reset/power-cycle again. Transfer control to the platform/BMC owner and invoke the pre-approved recovery path for the selected reset type using the recovery console. Preserve all logs/timelines and document every owner-directed recovery action.

source_conflict.reason: System Reset plus OS-IP in Procedure conflicts with BMC Reset plus BMC-IP in Criteria. Standards confirm separate system/manager reset resources; only project authority can select the intended physical control and oracle.

blocked.reason: The approval, monitoring, evidence and recovery framework are defined. Exact reset target/button, dual-plane states and deadline are owner-supplied Project inputs; execution remains gated but the test is not inherently impossible.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Written system-versus-BMC reset ruling; exact physical button/panel; expected OS-IP/BMC-IP/console/LED/service matrix; source 10-15 minute deadline disposition; target identities; workload drain/data protection; operator/observer; recovery/escalation procedure.
pending.execution_status: REVIEW COMPLETE BUT ENGINEERING DECISION PENDING; EXECUTION NOT STARTED; NO BUTTON PRESS, RESET, REBOOT, POWER CYCLE, LOG CLEAR, BMC/DUT OR OTHER HARDWARE ACTION AUTHORIZED OR EXECUTED

external_authorities.application: Separately defines ComputerSystem.Reset as resetting the system and Manager.Reset as resetting/rebooting the manager, supporting distinct host and management reset domains without selecting this platform's physical button.

project_authority: The platform/BMC owner selects the reset domain, exact button, dual-plane oracle and recovery deadline. The workload owner authorizes drain/data protection; an authorized operator performs one press; an independent observer captures the timeline. The end user decides verdict, and AI may not select a branch from the observed outage.
